title: Homogeneity Under Distribution Shift: Does Model Diversity Collapse on Out-of-Distribution Prompts?

original_idea.title: Homogeneity Under Distribution Shift: Does Model Diversity Collapse on Out-of-Distribution Prompts?
original_idea.problem: Models may appear diverse on standard benchmarks but converge on similar (often incorrect) responses when given out-of-distribution or adversarially shifted prompts.
original_idea.direction: Apply systematic prompt perturbations (paraphrase, domain shift, unusual formatting) to Infinity-Chat queries and measure whether inter-model similarity increases on OOD variants.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Safety failures often occur at distribution boundaries. If models converge precisely when inputs are novel or adversarial, the safety risk from homogeneity is concentrated at the most dangerous moments.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind methodology; OOD evaluation is standard in ML robustness literature; the combination has not been studied.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if models converge precisely when inputs are novel or adversarial, the safety risk from homogeneity is concentrated at the most dangerous moments. This is a critical finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: applying prompt perturbations and measuring similarity changes is feasible, though designing good OOD perturbations requires some care.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: comparison of homogeneity coefficients on standard vs. OOD-perturbed prompts, with clear numerical metrics.

novelty.reasoning: No existing study combines the Artificial Hivemind inter-model homogeneity measurement with OOD/adversarial prompt conditions. The RLHF diversity literature works at the single-model level. The specific hypothesis that homogeneity increases under distribution shift is untested and has direct safety implications.

evidence.finding: Measures homogeneity on standard queries but does not test OOD or adversarial inputs.

evidence.source: Understanding the Effects of RLHF on LLM Generalisation and Diversity (ICLR 2024)
evidence.finding: Studies OOD generalization vs diversity tradeoff in RLHF but at the single-model level, not inter-model homogeneity.
